title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (Word2Vec)
inputs: A large text corpus (tokenized into words), vocabulary size V, word sequences
outputs: D-dimensional continuous vector representations (embeddings) for each word in vocabulary
pseudocode:
1. Initialize word vectors W ∈ R^(V×D) randomly
2. Initialize context vectors C ∈ R^(V×D) randomly
3. For each epoch:
4.   For each word w_t in corpus:
5.     Get context window [w_{t-c}, ..., w_{t-1}, w_{t+1}, ..., w_{t+c}]
6.     SKIP-GRAM:
7.       For each context word w_c in window:
8.         Sample k negative words from noise distribution
9.         Compute σ(w_t^T · w_c) for positive pair
10.        Compute σ(-w_t^T · w_neg) for each negative sample
11.        Gradient ascent on log-likelihood objective
12.     OR CBOW:
13.       Average context vectors: h = (1/2c)Σ w_i
14.       Sample k negative words
15.       Predict center word w_t from context h
16.       Gradient ascent on log-likelihood objective
17.   Decay learning rate linearly
18. Return word vectors W
key_equations: Skip-gram objective: maximize Σ_t Σ_{-c≤j≤c,j≠0} log p(w_{t+j} | w_t)
p(w_O | w_I) = exp(v'_{w_O}^T v_{w_I}) / Σ_{w=1}^V exp(v'_w^T v_{w_I})
Negative sampling: log σ(v'_{w_O}^T v_{w_I}) + Σ_{i=1}^k E_{w_i~P_n(w)} [log σ(-v'_{w_i}^T v_{w_I})]
CBOW: maximize log p(w_t | w_{t-c},...,w_{t+c}) where context is averaged
Hierarchical softmax complexity: O(D × log_2(V)) vs full softmax O(D × V)
evaluation_dataset: Google News corpus (6B tokens, 1M vocabulary), Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test set (8869 semantic + 10675 syntactic questions), Microsoft Sentence Completion Challenge
toy_dataset_suggestion: text8 dataset (first 100MB of cleaned Wikipedia text, ~17M tokens) or a small synthetic corpus of 1-2M tokens with known semantic relationships (e.g., country-capital pairs, verb conjugations). Alternative: Penn Treebank or first 10k sentences of WikiText-2.
key_figure_description: A table or bar chart showing accuracy (%) on the Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test (or a subset) for different model architectures (NNLM, RNNLM, CBOW, Skip-gram) and different embedding dimensions (50, 100, 300). X-axis: model type or embedding dimension; Y-axis: accuracy percentage on semantic questions, syntactic questions, and total. Should show Skip-gram achieving highest semantic accuracy (~55%) and CBOW achieving highest syntactic accuracy (~64%).
notes: For toy implementation: (1) Use Skip-gram with negative sampling (simpler than hierarchical softmax). (2) Skip hierarchical softmax and use simple negative sampling with k=5-15. (3) Use smaller vocabulary (30k most frequent words). (4) Train for 1-3 epochs only. (5) Evaluate on a small subset of analogy questions (e.g., 100-500 questions). (6) Skip distributed training; single-threaded CPU implementation is sufficient. (7) Main goal: demonstrate that vector('king') - vector('man') + vector('woman') ≈ vector('queen') and similar analogies work after training. (8) Subsampling frequent words (like 'the', 'a') improves quality but can be skipped for minimal version.
